pr_title: Refactor Météo-France to use API instead of web scraping
pr_body:
<!--

## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->
The `meteo_france` integration moved from a web scraping architecture to a API based architecture. With this major refactor the following change could break something: 

- the `thunder chance` entity is no more available (no more in the API results)
- the `next rain` entity state is now a datetime instead of a delay
- `next rain` attributes have been simplified
- `weather_alert`: only one entity created by department. Was by city in the previous version and could create duplicates.
- `weather alert` attributes have been simplified
- `weather` platform is showing the current day forecast in first position of daily forecast (instead of tomorrow forecast)

## Proposed change
<!-- 
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
The previous integration violates ADR-0004 due to web scraping. With @Quentame we have rework it to use a REST API.
This new version is more simple to maintain, avoid crashing when source website is in maintenance or overloaded (previous issues already occured) and allows to search and select easily a city.

issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened instead.
-->

The Météo-France integration uses web scraping using BeautifulSoup, this violates [ADR-0004](https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/blob/master/adr/0004-webscraping.md).

The integration needs to either:

- Adjust, not to rely on web scraping.
- Deprecate, for 2 releases and remove it after that.

Code sample: <https://github.com/victorcerutti/meteofrance-py/blob/master/meteofrance/client.py#L102>

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant release with the issue: 0.105.4
- Last working Home Assistant release (if known): n/a
- Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.):  any
- Integration causing this issue: `meteo_france`
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/meteo_france/

## Additional information

[ADR-0004 - Webscraping](https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/blob/master/adr/0004-webscraping.md)
comments: Hey there @victorcerutti, @oncleben31, @Quentame, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`meteo_france`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L212) for? Thanks!

OK thanks for the warning. MeteoFrance doesn't provide a Public API, but uses a private one with their mobile app. Is it OK according to current rules or probable incoming ones if we develop a python module to reverse engineer the private API and use it to replace the web scraping?
We don't have policies around that. We currently only prohibit the use of web scraping, simply because they break so easily.
